## %CAR+ traceability chain (FC-CAR, release spec ≥20% of CD3+)

**Bottom line:** All five GMP PPQ runs passed the %CAR+ criterion. But the lowest %CAR+ results in the dataset trace to a vector storage excursion that the deviation record does not assess correctly, and the deviation's donor-based root cause is not supported by the data. The MOI change proposed in CC-26-022 would also breach the current MOI range control.

### 1. Process parameters that drive %CAR+
- **Transduction MOI (the main driver).** PPQ-001 CPP #1 sets MOI at 4.0–6.0 TU/cell. URS-EBR-009 and CS-EBR-03 hard-stop anything outside that range. The PD DoE shows a strong dose response (FC-CAR, mean of replicate runs):
  - MOI 2.5: 19–24%
  - MOI 5.0: 38–40%
  - MOI 10: 63–68%, with VCN/CAR 3.0–3.3
  - MOI 15: 75–77%, with VCN/CAR 4.7–5.0, close to the 5.0 limit
  - MOI 8 has not been tested.
- **Vector titer and storage.** Vector volume = MOI × cells ÷ CoA functional titer (CS-EBR-02). I checked the implied titer for every batch and it matches the CoA, so the calculation itself is correct. The titer is a static CoA value, so it does not reflect post-receipt degradation.
- **Other CPPs (PPQ-001):** seeding density 0.4–0.6 ×10⁶/mL, incubator 36.5–37.5 °C, culture 7–9 days, activation-to-transduction 20–30 h. Every batch was within range.

### 2. Risks threatening %CAR+ (val_risk_item, RA-PFMEA-001)
| Risk | Failure mode | RPN | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| FM-06 | MOI below target → low transduction | 128 (HIGH) | Control is "EBR calculation; CoA titer". This control cannot detect titer loss, which is the failure mode that occurred. |
| FM-05 | MOI above target → excess integrations, VCN | 108 | Linked to URS-EBR-009 |
| FM-07 | Vector held above −70 °C → loss of functional titer | 96 | Controls: ULT qualification, EMS alarms |
| FM-15 | OOS not flagged → non-conforming release (incl. %CAR+) | 80 | |
| FM-14 | VCN mis-calculated in LIMS | 90 | |
| FM-08 | Transduction outside 20–30 h | 54 | |
| FRA-042 / FRA-040 | MOI hard stop; vector volume calculation | (FRA, HIGH) | |

### 3. Controls, test evidence, and gaps
- **Controls:** URS-EBR-007 (vector volume calc), URS-EBR-009 (MOI range), CS-EBR-02/03 (calc and hard-stop configuration), SOP-MFG-104, LIMS validation, EMS alarms.
- **Test evidence:**
  - TC-OQ-EBR-04 (vector volume calc, PASS, TX-0083) covers URS-EBR-007 and CS-EBR-02 only.
  - TC-OQ-LIMS-04 (VCN calc, PASS) covers the LIMS VCN calculation.
  - TC-OQ-ULT and TC-PQ-ULT-01 cover freezer qualification.
- **Gaps:**
  1. **No test verifies the MOI 4–6 hard stop (URS-EBR-009 / CS-EBR-03).** The only linked test case has a 2.5–10 TU/cell test range, so it would not catch a hard-stop failure. FRA-042 is marked "SCRIPTED (robust)", but no test case is traced to it.
  2. **No assurance approach is recorded for any FM-xx PFMEA row**, including FM-06 and FM-07.
  3. **No post-storage functional titer re-test** is in place. The FM-06 control relies on the static CoA titer.
  4. **Alarm response gap on FRZ-80-02.** The high-temperature alarm (EV-26-0009) fired at 03:20 on 20-Apr but was acknowledged at 14:40 by warehouse staff. FRA-027 requires escalation of unacknowledged critical alarms.

### 4. Measurement and validation
- **Method:** AM-FC-CAR (flow cytometry, range 5–90% of CD3+) is validated under AMV-FC-CAR-01 (TC-AMV-CAR-01, TX-0086, PASS).
- **Spec:** QC release FC-CAR ≥20% of CD3+; VCN-PER-CAR ≤5.0 copies/CAR+ cell (AM-VCN validated, TX-0087).
- **PPQ criteria:** PPQ-001 CQA #8 (CAR ≥20%) and CQA #9 (VCN ≤5.0). PPQ-001 is "EXECUTION COMPLETE – REPORT PENDING", so it is not yet approved.

### 5. PPQ performance
| Batch | Vector lot | FC-CAR (%) | VCN/CAR | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PPQ26-01 | LV26-007 | 44.6 | 2.39 | PASS |
| PPQ26-02 | LV26-007 | 39.2 | 2.23 | PASS |
| PPQ26-03 | LV26-007 | 36.1 | 1.79 | PASS |
| PPQ26-04 | LV26-021 | 38.9 | 1.87 | PASS |
| PPQ26-05 | LV26-021 | 37.3 | 2.22 | PASS |

Engineering runs ENG26-01/02/03 (LV25-118, not GMP) gave 19.8, 11.9 and 13.9%. All three were flagged "NONCONFORMING (INFO)". None of the PPQ batches used LV25-118.

### 6. Deviations, change controls and CAPAs, and how they connect
- **DEV-26-021 (MAJOR, closed 12-May):** FRZ-80-02 compressor failure. The vector lots stored there were exposed.
  - My reading of the freezer trace (hist_tag_data): FRZ-80-02 rose above −65 °C at about 05:00 on 20-Apr and did not return below −65 °C until about 13:00 on 23-Apr. It peaked near −10 °C.
  - The deviation describes the excursion as "short" with a maximum of about −36 °C and relocation at 15:30 on 20-Apr. The trace does not support that.
  - The lot master still lists LV25-118 in FRZ-80-02 and it remains RELEASED. The deviation has no trace link to LV25-118 or to the affected batches.
- **DEV-26-027 (MINOR, OPEN):** Low %CAR+ in ENG26-01/02, attributed to low donor CD3%. This attribution does not fit the data:
  - Aphaeresis CD3 for ENG26-01/02 was 65.3% and 63.8%, higher than the conforming PPQ26-02 and -04 batches.
  - ENG26-03 is not covered by the deviation, even though it also failed.
- **Likely root cause (hypothesis, needs confirmation):** The low runs are PD26-024/025/026/027 and ENG26-01/02/03. All used LV25-118 transduced after the excursion and gave 11.9–19.8% CAR+ (PD26-024 to -027: 14.9–17.3%; ENG runs: 11.9–19.8%). The same lot transduced before the excursion (PD26-014 to -023) gave 34.5–41.3%. The post-excursion VCN/CAR of 1.2–1.6 is consistent with an effective MOI near 2–2.5 (per the DoE), which suggests the functional titer dropped by roughly half. Incubator (INC-PD-01 and three different ENG incubators), seeding, and activation lots do not separate the groups. PPQ and other conforming runs used LV26-007 or LV26-021, which were stored in FRZ-80-01.
- **CAPA-26-016 (PD, OPEN, due 30-Sep):** Evaluate a minimum CD3% acceptance criterion at apheresis. This CAPA is aimed at the donor hypothesis, which the data does not support.
- **CAPA-26-008 (CLOSED):** Compressor replacement, marked "effective – no recurrence". It does not address the vector lot exposure.
- **CC-26-022 (MAJOR, open, impact assessment):** Raise target MOI from 5.0 to 8.0 TU/cell to improve %CAR+. The change is not yet assessed against the constraints it would break:
  - It would exceed the URS-EBR-009 / CS-EBR-03 hard stop (4–6 TU/cell).
  - It would breach PPQ-001 CPP #1.
  - The VCN/CAR rise at MOI 10–15 (up to 4.7–5.0) makes the 5.0 VCN limit a concern.
  - It is traced only to SOP-MFG-104. It is not traced to URS-EBR-009, CS-EBR-03, PPQ-001, FRA-042, or FM-05/06.
- **Other PPQ deviation (not CAR-related):** DEV-26-033 (PPQ26-02 harvest viability 75.2% vs the 80% criterion, caused by INC-03 door left unlatched). CAPA-26-015 is closed. It is linked to P

content.text:
## %CAR+ traceability chain (FC-CAR, release spec ≥20% of CD3+)

**Bottom line:** All five GMP PPQ runs passed the %CAR+ criterion. But the lowest %CAR+ results in the dataset trace to a vector storage excursion that the deviation record does not assess correctly, and the deviation's donor-based root cause is not supported by the data. The MOI change proposed in CC-26-022 would also breach the current MOI range control.

### 1. Process parameters that drive %CAR+
- **Transduction MOI (the main driver).** PPQ-001 CPP #1 sets MOI at 4.0–6.0 TU/cell. URS-EBR-009 and CS-EBR-03 hard-stop anything outside that range. The PD DoE shows a strong dose response (FC-CAR, mean of replicate runs):
  - MOI 2.5: 19–24%
  - MOI 5.0: 38–40%
  - MOI 10: 63–68%, with VCN/CAR 3.0–3.3
  - MOI 15: 75–77%, with VCN/CAR 4.7–5.0, close to the 5.0 limit
  - MOI 8 has not been tested.
- **Vector titer and storage.** Vector volume = MOI × cells ÷ CoA functional titer (CS-EBR-02). I checked the implied titer for every batch and it matches the CoA, so the calculation itself is correct. The titer is a static CoA value, so it does not reflect post-receipt degradation.
- **Other CPPs (PPQ-001):** seeding density 0.4–0.6 ×10⁶/mL, incubator 36.5–37.5 °C, culture 7–9 days, activation-to-transduction 20–30 h. Every batch was within range.

### 2. Risks threatening %CAR+ (val_risk_item, RA-PFMEA-001)
| Risk | Failure mode | RPN | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| FM-06 | MOI below target → low transduction | 128 (HIGH) | Control is "EBR calculation; CoA titer". This control cannot detect titer loss, which is the failure mode that occurred. |
| FM-05 | MOI above target → excess integrations, VCN | 108 | Linked to URS-EBR-009 |
| FM-07 | Vector held above −70 °C → loss of functional titer | 96 | Controls: ULT qualification, EMS alarms |
| FM-15 | OOS not flagged → non-conforming release (incl. %CAR+) | 80 | |
| FM-14 | VCN mis-calculated in LIMS | 90 | |
| FM-08 | Transduction outside 20–30 h | 54 | |
| FRA-042 / FRA-040 | MOI hard stop; vector volume calculation | (FRA, HIGH) | |

### 3. Controls, test evidence, and gaps
- **Controls:** URS-EBR-007 (vector volume calc), URS-EBR-009 (MOI range), CS-EBR-02/03 (calc and hard-stop configuration), SOP-MFG-104, LIMS validation, EMS alarms.
- **Test evidence:**
  - TC-OQ-EBR-04 (vector volume calc, PASS, TX-0083) covers URS-EBR-007 and CS-EBR-02 only.
  - TC-OQ-LIMS-04 (VCN calc, PASS) covers the LIMS VCN calculation.
  - TC-OQ-ULT and TC-PQ-ULT-01 cover freezer qualification.
- **Gaps:**
  1. **No test verifies the MOI 4–6 hard stop (URS-EBR-009 / CS-EBR-03).** The only linked test case has a 2.5–10 TU/cell test range, so it would not catch a hard-stop failure. FRA-042 is marked "SCRIPTED (robust)", but no test case is traced to it.
  2. **No assurance approach is recorded for any FM-xx PFMEA row**, including FM-06 and FM-07.
  3. **No post-storage functional titer re-test** is in place. The FM-06 control relies on the static CoA titer.
  4. **Alarm response gap on FRZ-80-02.** The high-temperature alarm (EV-26-0009) fired at 03:20 on 20-Apr but was acknowledged at 14:40 by warehouse staff. FRA-027 requires escalation of unacknowledged critical alarms.

### 4. Measurement and validation
- **Method:** AM-FC-CAR (flow cytometry, range 5–90% of CD3+) is validated under AMV-FC-CAR-01 (TC-AMV-CAR-01, TX-0086, PASS).
- **Spec:** QC release FC-CAR ≥20% of CD3+; VCN-PER-CAR ≤5.0 copies/CAR+ cell (AM-VCN validated, TX-0087).
- **PPQ criteria:** PPQ-001 CQA #8 (CAR ≥20%) and CQA #9 (VCN ≤5.0). PPQ-001 is "EXECUTION COMPLETE – REPORT PENDING", so it is not yet approved.

### 5. PPQ performance
| Batch | Vector lot | FC-CAR (%) | VCN/CAR | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PPQ26-01 | LV26-007 | 44.6 | 2.39 | PASS |
| PPQ26-02 | LV26-007 | 39.2 | 2.23 | PASS |
| PPQ26-03 | LV26-007 | 36.1 | 1.79 | PASS |
| PPQ26-04 | LV26-021 | 38.9 | 1.87 | PASS |
| PPQ26-05 | LV26-021 | 37.3 | 2.22 | PASS |

Engineering runs ENG26-01/02/03 (LV25-118, not GMP) gave 19.8, 11.9 and 13.9%. All three were flagged "NONCONFORMING (INFO)". None of the PPQ batches used LV25-118.

### 6. Deviations, change controls and CAPAs, and how they connect
- **DEV-26-021 (MAJOR, closed 12-May):** FRZ-80-02 compressor failure. The vector lots stored there were exposed.
  - My reading of the freezer trace (hist_tag_data): FRZ-80-02 rose above −65 °C at about 05:00 on 20-Apr and did not return below −65 °C until about 13:00 on 23-Apr. It peaked near −10 °C.
  - The deviation describes the excursion as "short" with a maximum of about −36 °C and relocation at 15:30 on 20-Apr. The trace does not support that.
  - The lot master still lists LV25-118 in FRZ-80-02 and it remains RELEASED. The deviation has no trace link to LV25-118 or to the affected batches.
- **DEV-26-027 (MINOR, OPEN):** Low %CAR+ in ENG26-01/02, attributed to low donor CD3%. This attribution does not fit the data:
  - Aphaeresis CD3 for ENG26-01/02 was 65.3% and 63.8%, higher than the conforming PPQ26-02 and -04 batches.
  - ENG26-03 is not covered by the deviation, even though it also failed.
- **Likely root cause (hypothesis, needs confirmation):** The low runs are PD26-024/025/026/027 and ENG26-01/02/03. All used LV25-118 transduced after the excursion and gave 11.9–19.8% CAR+ (PD26-024 to -027: 14.9–17.3%; ENG runs: 11.9–19.8%). The same lot transduced before the excursion (PD26-014 to -023) gave 34.5–41.3%. The post-excursion VCN/CAR of 1.2–1.6 is consistent with an effective MOI near 2–2.5 (per the DoE), which suggests the functional titer dropped by roughly half. Incubator (INC-PD-01 and three different ENG incubators), seeding, and activation lots do not separate the groups. PPQ and other conforming runs used LV26-007 or LV26-021, which were stored in FRZ-80-01.
- **CAPA-26-016 (PD, OPEN, due 30-Sep):** Evaluate a minimum CD3% acceptance criterion at apheresis. This CAPA is aimed at the donor hypothesis, which the data does not support.
- **CAPA-26-008 (CLOSED):** Compressor replacement, marked "effective – no recurrence". It does not address the vector lot exposure.
- **CC-26-022 (MAJOR, open, impact assessment):** Raise target MOI from 5.0 to 8.0 TU/cell to improve %CAR+. The change is not yet assessed against the constraints it would break:
  - It would exceed the URS-EBR-009 / CS-EBR-03 hard stop (4–6 TU/cell).
  - It would breach PPQ-001 CPP #1.
  - The VCN/CAR rise at MOI 10–15 (up to 4.7–5.0) makes the 5.0 VCN limit a concern.
  - It is traced only to SOP-MFG-104. It is not traced to URS-EBR-009, CS-EBR-03, PPQ-001, FRA-042, or FM-05/06.
